name: Acehnese
orthography_note: Thurgood's transcription, respelled in IPA here: his y is j, j is ɟ, ñ is ɲ, č is t͡ʃ, ts is t͡s, ph th kh are pʰ tʰ kʰ, bh dh gh are bʱ dʱ ɡʱ; c is kept. The printed form is in source_form.
notes: Thurgood's column 'Aceh.'. In his classification (1999: 36, Figure 6): a branch of its own, drawn with a broken line; it 'left the mainland before the bulk of the changes began' (p. 68). Proto-Acehnese is Durie's reconstruction. Entered straight under Proto-Chamic, without Thurgood's subgroups as nodes (decision thurgood1999-tree). Glottocode, ISO code and coordinates from Glottolog 5.4. Acehnese lowers the Proto-Chamic high vowels, and lowers nasalized vowels further (pp. 114, 120-121).
inherit_note: Thurgood's summary tables give the reflexes of the Proto-Chamic consonants and of the basic main-syllable vowels (Tables 12-45, 52, 57, 59, 63, 65). The reflexes of each rime (Tables 56, 58, 62, 71, 82-88), of the length contrasts, of *ə and *ɔ and of the presyllable vowels are not entered: what has no row is assumed unchanged, which is certainly too little for the vowels.

Thurgood writes a dot under a voiceless stop that goes back to a voiced one (p̣, ṭ, ḳ, c̣): the following vowel has the breathy second register (a low tone in Phan Rang).
